## Scope of this Part

## 77.1

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.1] This Part contains rules about –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.1] (a) in Section 1, applications for a serious crime prevention order under section 8 of the Serious Crime Act 2007 1 and related applications under sections 9, 17 and 18 of that Act; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.1] (b) in Section 2, applications under section 54(3) of the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996 2 for an order quashing an acquittal. ## I SERIOUS CRIME PREVENTION ORDERS

## Interpretation

## 77.1A

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.1A] In this Section –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.1A] (a) ‘the 2007 Act’ means the Serious Crime Act 2007; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.1A] (b) ‘SCPO’ means a serious crime prevention order under section 1 or section 9 of the 2007 Act. ## Application for a SCPO

## 77.2

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.2] An application under section 8 of the 2007 Act for a SCPO must be started in accordance with Part 8 as modified by Practice Direction 77. ## 77.3

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.3] An application under –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.3] (a) section 9 of the 2007 Act; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.3] (b) section 17 or 18 of the 2007 Act to vary or discharge a SCPO made by the High Court,

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.3] must be made in accordance with Part 23 as modified by Practice Direction 77. ## Application to vary or discharge a SCPO made by the Crown Court

## 77.4

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.4] An application under section 17 or 18 of the 2007 Act to vary or discharge a SCPO made by the Crown Court must be started in accordance with Part 8. ## Where to make an application

## 77.5

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.5] Applications under this Part must be made to the Administrative Court in accordance with Practice Direction 77. ## II APPLICATION TO QUASH AN ACQUITTAL

## Scope and interpretation

## 77.6

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (1) This Section contains rules about applications to quash an acquittal under section 54(3) of the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996 3 and applies in relation to acquittals in respect of offences alleged to have been committed on or after 15th April 1997. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (2) An application made under this Section may be made only by the individual or body which acted as prosecutor in the proceedings which led to the acquittal. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (3) In this Section –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (a) ‘the 1996 Act’ means the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (b) ‘acquitted person’ means a person whose acquittal of an offence is the subject of a certification under section 54(2) of the 1996 Act, and ‘acquittal’ means the acquittal of that person of that offence;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (c) ‘magistrates’ court’ has the same meaning as in section 148 of the Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980 4 ; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (d) ‘record of court proceedings’ means –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (i) where the proceedings took place in the Crown Court, a transcript of the evidence; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] (ii) where the proceedings took place in a magistrates’ court, a transcript of the evidence if there is one and if not a note of the evidence made by the justices’ clerk,

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.6] in the proceedings which led to the conviction for the administration of justice offence referred to in section 54(1)(b) of the 1996 Act or, as the case may be, the proceedings which led to the acquittal. ## Time limit for making the application

## 77.7

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.7] An application for an order quashing an acquittal under section 54(3) of the 1996 Act must be made no later than 28 days after the issue of the certificate to which section 54(2) of that Act refers. ## Where to make the application

## 77.8

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.8] (1) The jurisdiction of the High Court under section 54(3) of the 1996 Act may be exercised by a Divisional Court or a single judge of the High Court. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.8] (2) The application must be made to the Administrative Court which will direct whether the application should be dealt with by a Divisional Court or a single judge of the High Court. ## How to make the application

## 77.9

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.9] (1) The application must be made by filing a claim form pursuant to Part 8. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.9] (2) The claimant must file with the claim form –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.9] (a) a witness statement which deals with the conditions in section 55(1), (2) and (4) of the 1996 Act and which exhibits any relevant documents (which may include a copy of any record of court proceedings); and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.9] (b) a copy of the certification under section 54(2) of the 1996 Act. ## Notice to defendant (acquitted person)

## 77.10

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (1) Within 7 days of the claim form being issued by the court, the claimant must serve on the defendant (the acquitted person) a copy of the claim form and the documents which accompanied it. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (2) The documents referred to in paragraph (1) must be accompanied by a notice informing the defendant that –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (a) the result of the application may be the making of an order by the High Court quashing the acquittal; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (b) the defendant must, if wishing to respond to the application, file –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (i) within 14 days of service of the claim form an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (ii) within 28 days of service of the claim form any witness statement on which the defendant wishes to rely. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.10] (3) The claimant must file as soon as practicable after service of the notice on the defendant a certificate of service together with a copy of the notice. ## Response to the application

## 77.11

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (1) The defendant must, if wishing to respond to the application, file –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (a) an acknowledgment of service within 14 days of service of the claim form under rule 77.10; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (b) a witness statement which –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (i) deals with the conditions in section 55(1), (2) and (4) of the 1996 Act; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (ii) exhibits any relevant documents (which may include a copy of any record of court proceedings),

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] within 28 days of service of the claim form under rule 77.10. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (2) The defendant must serve the documents in paragraph (1) on the claimant within 7 days of filing them with the court. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.11] (3) Rule 8.5(3) does not apply. ## Further evidence

## 77.12

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.12] (1) The claimant may, not later than 10 days after the expiry of the period allowed in rule 77.11(1), apply without notice for permission to file further evidence. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.12] (2) Any order granting permission to file further evidence will specify the period within which that further evidence is to be filed. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.12] (3) The claimant must serve a copy of the further evidence on the defendant within 4 days of filing that further evidence. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.12] (4) Rule 8.5(5) and 8.5(6) do not apply. ## Determination of the application to quash an acquittal (general provisions)

## 77.13

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (1) The application to quash an acquittal will be determined without a hearing unless the court, of its own initiative or on the application by a party, orders otherwise. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (2) The determination of the application to quash an acquittal will not be made, and any hearing of the application (if ordered) will not take place, before the expiry of –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (a) 10 days after the expiry of the period allowed under rule 77.11(1); or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (b) 10 days after the expiry of the period allowed by any order made under rule 77.12(2). [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (3) The court will serve notice of any order made on the application to quash an acquittal on the parties and where the court before which the acquittal or conviction occurred was –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (a) a magistrates’ court, on the designated officer; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.13] (b) the Crown Court, on the appropriate officer of the Crown Court sitting at the place where the acquittal or conviction occurred. ## Application for a hearing to determine the application to quash an acquittal

## 77.14

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (1) An application for a hearing under rule 77.13(1) must –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (a) be made no later than 7 days after the expiry of the period allowed –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (i) under rule 77.11(1); or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (ii) by any order made under rule 77.12(2); and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (b) state whether a hearing is requested in order for a witness for the other party to attend to be cross-examined (GL) and, if so, the reasons for wishing the witness to attend. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (2) The party applying for a hearing must –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (a) serve a copy of the application notice on the other party within 4 days of filing it with the court; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (b) file a certificate of service. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (3) The party served with an application for a hearing must file any representations within 5 days of service of the application notice. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (4) Subject to paragraph (5), the court will not determine an application for a hearing unless a certificate of service has been filed pursuant to sub-paragraph (2)(b) and –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (a) representations have been filed under paragraph (3); or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (b) the period for filing representations under paragraph (3) has expired. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (5) Where –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (a) no certificate of service has been filed; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] (b) no representations under paragraph (3) have been received after the expiry of 7 days from the date of filing the application,

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.14] the court may dismiss the application for a hearing. ## Hearing to determine the application to quash an acquittal

## 77.15

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] Where a hearing is ordered, the court –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] (a) may order a witness to attend to be cross-examined (GL) –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] (i) of its own initiative; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] (ii) on a without notice application by a party; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] (b) will serve a notice on all parties setting out –

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] (i) the date, time and place of the hearing; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.15] (ii) the details of any witness ordered to attend for cross-examination (GL) . ## SECTION 3 Referral of Release Decisions

## SUB-SECTION 1 General

## Scope

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Scope] 77.16. This Section applies where the Secretary of State directs the Parole Board to refer a release decision to the High Court under section 32ZAA of the Crime (Sentences) Act 1997 (“the 1997 Act”) or section 256AZBA of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (“the 2003 Act”). ## Part 8 procedure

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Part 8 procedure] 77.17. The Part 8 procedure applies to proceedings under this Section with the following modifications. ## Proceedings under this Section

## 77.18. In proceedings under this Section—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.18. In proceedings under this Section—] (a)the referral of a release decision shall be treated as an application by the Secretary of State;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.18. In proceedings under this Section—] (b)the Secretary of State is the claimant;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.18. In proceedings under this Section—] (c)the prisoner is the defendant;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.18. In proceedings under this Section—] (d)the Parole Board and any victim (as defined in section 1 of the Victims and Prisoners Act 2024) of an offence to which the referral relates are not parties;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.18. In proceedings under this Section—] (e)rules 8.7 and 8.8 shall not apply. ## The application

## 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (a)state that the Parole Board has been directed by the claimant to refer the release decision to the court because the claimant considers that—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (i)the release of the defendant would be likely to undermine public confidence in the parole system; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (ii)if the case were referred, the High Court might not be satisfied that it is no longer necessary for the protection of the public that the defendant should be confined;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (b)identify the provisions in the 1997 Act or the 2003 Act under which the direction was made; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (c)state that the claimant will file and serve all further material in accordance with paragraph (2). [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (2) Rule 8.5(1) is modified such that, not later than two days after the date on which the claim form is filed, the claimant must file with the court and, together with the claim form, serve on the defendant—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (a)the claimant’s reasons for considering why the court might not be satisfied that it is no longer necessary for the protection of the public that the defendant should be confined;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (b)any representations regarding the directions the court may include as to the conditions to be included in the defendant’s licence on release;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (c)the Parole Board’s decision letter;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (d)all information and reports served on and considered by the Parole Board; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (e)any further information the claimant considers relevant to the application. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (3) Paragraph (2) is subject to rule 77.21. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (4) In any proceedings under this Section, the claimant may not rely on any written evidence or information unless—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (a)it has been served in accordance with—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (i)a rule or practice direction under this Section; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (ii)a direction of the court; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (b)the court gives permission. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (5) Without prejudice to Sub-section 2, until the proceedings to which this Section applies are concluded, the claimant must file and serve on the defendant any material which—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (a)adversely affects the claimant’s case; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.19. —(1) The claim form must—] (b)supports the defendant’s case. ## Service on the defendant

## 77.20. —(1) Except where rule 6.7 applies—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.20. —(1) Except where rule 6.7 applies—] (a)the claim form must be served personally in accordance with rule 6.5; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.20. —(1) Except where rule 6.7 applies—] (b)the time within which a certificate of service must be filed under rule 6.17(2)(a) shall be within 7 days of service of the claim form. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.20. —(1) Except where rule 6.7 applies—] (2) Except where the defendant has given an address for service under rule 6.23(2)(a), a document other than the claim form must be served on the defendant personally in accordance with rule 6.22. ## SUB-SECTION 2 Non-disclosure

## Applications for non-disclosure

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Applications for non-disclosure] 77.21. Any application under section 6(2) of the Justice and Security Act 2013 (“the 2013 Act”) or rule 77.23 must be made—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Applications for non-disclosure] (a)when the claimant files material under rule 77.19(2); or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Applications for non-disclosure] (b)if they have filed their material under rule 77.19(2), when the claimant files any additional material in respect of which they wish to make an application. ## Applications under Part 2 of the 2013 Act

## 77.22. Where Part 2 of the 2013 Act applies to proceedings under this Section, Part 82 shall apply. ## Applications other than under Part 2 of the 2013 Act

## 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—] (a)the disclosure of any information or any report (“the relevant material”) would adversely affect—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—] (i)the prevention of disorder or crime; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—] (ii)the health or welfare of the defendant or any other person; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—] (b)withholding the relevant material is a necessary and proportionate measure. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—] (2) Where this rule applies, the court must direct that the relevant material—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.23. —(1) This rule applies where, on application by the claimant, the court considers that—] (a)be withheld from the defendant and their legal representative;
